source: Real PET images from TCIA collections (see sources); tools/make_real_pet.py

real-pet-suv.label: The CT, the PET in standardized uptake value, and the PET/CT fusion of one axial slice through a lung tumour
real-pet-suv.cap: One axial slice of a real FDG PET/CT of a patient with a lung tumour (GE Discovery STE): the CT, the PET (dark is high uptake, scale 0 to SUV 10), and the PET in colour over the CT. The PET is resampled onto the CT grid. Data: TCIA NSCLC Radiogenomics (CC BY 3.0).

views.label: PET/CT
views.facts: Header values: 100 kg, 613 MBq injected, scanned 77 min later, half-life 109.8 min, so 377 MBq remain at the scan. A concentration of 134 kBq/mL in the tumour is SUV 35.7 (SUV = concentration × weight / remaining activity). The lung on the other side averages SUV 0.6. The PET pixels are 5.5 mm and the CT pixels 0.98 mm.

real-pet-ac.label: Real FDG PET of a patient with a lung tumour reconstructed without and with attenuation correction, as a coronal maximum-intensity projection and as an axial slice
real-pet-ac.cap: One real FDG PET scan of a patient with a lung tumour (GE Discovery STE), reconstructed twice from the same data: without attenuation correction (left) and with CT-based attenuation correction (right). Dark is high uptake. Data: TCIA NSCLC Radiogenomics (CC BY 3.0).
real-pet-ac.head: View

views.label: Coronal MIP
views.facts: The corrected series lists attenuation (ATTN) and scatter (SCAT) correction in its DICOM header, and the uncorrected one lists neither. Without correction the liver almost disappears, and the surface of the body and the arms look hot.

views.label: Axial slice
views.facts: At the level of the tumour, without correction the skin is outlined by a bright rim, the interior is noisy, and streaks distort the tumour. Photons from deep sites are attenuated more, so fewer of them are counted, and the deep tissue is under-represented.

real-pet-tracers.label: Coronal maximum-intensity projections of real PET scans with three F-18 tracers: FDG, sodium fluoride, and PSMA
real-pet-tracers.cap: Real coronal MIPs of three patients, each scanned with an F-18 tracer: FDG (a patient with a lung tumour), sodium fluoride (a patient from a prostate cancer study), and a PSMA ligand (a patient from a prostate cancer study; the head is blank in these images as released). Dark is high uptake. Data: TCIA NSCLC Radiogenomics (CC BY 3.0), NaF PROSTATE (CC BY 3.0), and PSMA-PET-CT-Lesions (CC BY 4.0).

views.label: Tracers
views.facts: All three tracers carry F-18, with a half-life of 110 min, but they follow different processes, so the pictures differ. FDG (glucose use) shows the brain, the kidneys, the bladder, and the tumour. Sodium fluoride (bone formation) shows the skeleton, with excretion through the kidneys and bladder. The PSMA ligand shows the kidneys, the liver, the spleen, the bowel, the bladder, and the lesions.
